newsitem.title: USA: Clinton names Gambling Commission appointees.
newsitem.headline: Clinton names Gambling Commission appointees.

text.p: President Clinton plans to appoint a Nevada gaming regulator, a former New Jersey state treasurer and an American Indian to a new nine-member gambling commission, the White House said Tuesday.

Clinton's choices were William Bible, who chairs the Nevada State Gaming Control Board; Richard Leone, a former New Jersey state treasurer who is president of the Twentieth Century Fund, and Robert Loescher, a leader of Alaska's Tlingit Indian Tribe.

Clinton chose the three because he "wants a balanced study of the impact of legalised gambling on the U.S. economy and society at large," a White House official said. They will join six others already named to the panel by Republican House Speaker Newt Gingrich and Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott.

Bible favours legalised gambling, while Leone and Loescher are known to be personally opposed. Clinton tried to balance the congressional appointments to assure the commission "really does take into account a variety of points of view," White House spokesman Mike McCurry said.
"As you know, two of the three nominees that the president has now put forward are more associated with the views that are sceptical about gambling," McCurry said.

The gambling industry opposed the legislation that created the commission. It was sponsored by Republican Representative Frank Wolf of Virginia, an opponent of gambling who wanted a study of whether gambling is economically and socially desirable.
The commission will conduct a two-year, $5 million probe of the benefits and liabilities of casino gambling, state-sponsored lotteries, horse racing and sports betting.

Wolf sharply criticised Clinton's choices in a House speech, saying, "The president's appointments, in my opinion, tilt the balance of the commission in favour of the gambling industry." He said Clinton was influenced by campaign contributions from gambling interests.
"The president has turned his back on all those desperate Americans addicted to gambling," Wolf charged.

But McCurry said, "We are confident that these members can fulfil the terms on which the commission was established to take a good, honest and thorough look at the status of legalised gambling and its impact on our society.".
